subject: fix(replay): never chain a record onto a head we cannot name
instruction:
fix(replay): never chain a record onto a head we cannot name

`sync/1`'s comment promised the journal would refuse to append onto a file
whose tail it could not read; the code appended anyway, which would have
produced a record that looks chained and is not — worse than a stated gap,
because a verifier would report it as tampering rather than as loss.

A handle now carries `synced?`, and an append on an unsynced handle retries
the tail read first (the failure may have been transient) and stages a gap
without writing if it still cannot name the head. `sync/1` keeps clearing
`degraded?` because that is what opens a writing window, but the internal
resync does not, so an append that recovers mid-turn cannot un-announce a
degradation the caller already reported.

Also drops the unused `kinds/0` vocabulary accessor rather than shipping
public surface nothing consumes.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - a handle whose tail cannot be read stages a gap instead of forging a link

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends, applied to a fresh checkout of the starting commit. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place, but they are yours: they are not copied into the tree the grade runs in. The change is collected as a diff over `lib/`, `assets/`, `priv/`, `config/`, `docs/` and `README.md`; a change to any other path — `mix.exs` and `.formatter.exs` included — is refused rather than graded. Work only inside this worktree.
